body:
A vape that is cleaned regularly tastes better, leaks less, charges more reliably and lasts longer than one that is allowed to collect residue, lint and spilled liquid. Cleaning is not complicated, but it is easy to do wrongly: water on the wrong part, metal tools in the wrong port or a coil rinsed when it should have been replaced. This guide explains what to clean and what never to clean, how to clean each type of device, which tools to use, how often to clean, how to clean tanks and pods, how to deal with spilled liquid, how to clean charging ports and contacts, how to dry parts, what to avoid and how to build a routine. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive, liquid should be kept away from children and pets and nothing here is medical advice.

## Why cleaning matters
Liquid is sticky. Spilled drops, condensation and residue collect on the mouthpiece, the base, the contacts and in the airflow channel. Over time, that residue dulls flavor, blocks airflow, causes poor electrical contact and can lead to leaks and misfires. Lint from pockets clogs charging ports. A few minutes of cleaning each week prevents most of these problems, and it keeps the device pleasant to hold and to use.

## What you need
- **Paper towels or a lint-free cloth.**
- **Dry cotton buds.**
- **A wooden toothpick,** for lint in ports.
- **Warm water,** for refillable tank parts that can be rinsed.
- **A little mild dish soap,** optional, for glass or plastic tank parts.
- **A clean, dry place** to let parts air-dry.

Do not use metal tools, harsh chemicals, strong solvents or compressed air at high pressure. They can damage parts or push debris deeper.

## What never to clean with water
Never wet the battery section, the electronics, the charging port or the contacts, and never submerge a device. Do not rinse a coil, a pod with an attached coil or a sealed disposable. Water and electronics do not mix, and moisture in the wrong place can cause shorts or corrosion. If a part cannot be separated from the battery, wipe it with a dry or very slightly damp cloth, and let it dry.

## Cleaning a disposable
Disposables are sealed. Wipe the outside with a dry cloth, clean the mouthpiece with a dry cotton bud and clear lint from the charging port with a toothpick, gently, with the device off. Do not open it, and do not put it in water. Store it upright. When it is finished, take it for recycling.

## Cleaning a pod system
1. Remove the pod, and switch the device off.
2. Wipe the outside of the pod and the device with a dry cloth.
3. Clean the metal contacts on the pod and the battery with a dry cotton bud.
4. Check the airflow holes, and clear lint with a toothpick, gently.
5. Wipe the mouthpiece.
6. Let everything dry for a few minutes before you reassemble.

Closed pods are not cleaned inside; replace them when flavor fades. Refillable pods can be emptied and wiped, but the coil should be replaced when worn. See [how to change a pod or coil](/blog/how-to-change-a-pod-or-coil/).

## Cleaning a tank
1. Remove the tank from the device, and empty any liquid.
2. Disassemble the parts that come apart: mouthpiece, glass, base and seals. Remove the coil.
3. Rinse the glass, the mouthpiece and the metal parts in warm water. Use a drop of mild soap if needed, and rinse well.
4. Do not rinse the coil. Replace it if it is worn.
5. Dry the parts with a lint-free cloth and let them air-dry fully.
6. Check the O-rings for cracks or hardening. Replace them if needed.
7. Reassemble, fit a new or primed coil and refill.

Moisture left in a tank can dilute liquid and affect flavor, so make sure it is completely dry.

## Cleaning contacts and ports
The contacts between the battery and the pod or tank, and the charging port, are where residue and lint cause trouble. With the device off, wipe contacts with a dry cotton bud. For the charging port, use a wooden toothpick to lift lint, and do not push into the pins. Never use metal tools. If a contact looks corroded, replace the part, and do not charge a device with a damp or corroded port.

## Cleaning up spilled liquid
Wipe spills at once with paper towels, wearing gloves if you can, and wash your hands and the surface afterward. Avoid skin contact. Dispose of the towels responsibly. Keep liquid away from children and pets while you clean. If liquid has reached the charging port, do not charge until it is dry. See [leaking causes and fixes](/blog/vape-leaking-causes-and-fixes/) and [keeping vapes away from children and pets](/blog/keeping-vapes-away-from-children-and-pets/).

## How often to clean
- **Daily:** wipe the mouthpiece and the outside if they are sticky.
- **Weekly:** clean contacts, check airflow holes and wipe the base.
- **When you change a coil or pod:** clean the tank or pod seat and contacts.
- **Monthly:** check ports, seals and O-rings, and give tanks a full rinse.

A short, regular routine beats an occasional deep clean.

## A worked example
Your tank has started to taste flat and gurgle. You empty it, take it apart and find sticky residue in the base and a hardened O-ring. You rinse the glass and the base in warm water, dry them, replace the O-ring and fit a new, primed coil. You wipe the contacts with a cotton bud. After refilling and resting for ten minutes, the flavor is back, and the gurgle is gone. The whole job took fifteen minutes, and the parts you replaced cost a few dollars.

## Drying and reassembly
Let all rinsed parts air-dry for at least an hour, or longer if possible. Do not use a hairdryer or an oven, because heat can warp parts. Reassemble when everything is dry, and check that threads are clean and seals sit properly. Do not overtighten.

## What to avoid
- **Soaking batteries or electronics.**
- **Rinsing coils.**
- **Metal tools in ports.**
- **Strong solvents or alcohol on plastics,** which can crack them.
- **Dry burning a coil to clean it,** which can damage the coil and device.
- **Forcing stuck parts.**

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Can I clean a pod and reuse it?
Refillable pods can be wiped and refilled, but the coil wears out. Replace the pod or coil when flavor fades.

### Can I use alcohol wipes?
Avoid them on plastics, and never on electronics. A dry cloth is the better choice for most parts.

### How do I clean the mouthpiece?
Wipe with a dry cloth or cotton bud. For tank mouthpieces that detach, rinse in warm water and dry.

### What if my device smells odd after cleaning?
Make sure everything is dry. If a smell persists, or the device is hot, stop using it and recycle it.

### Should I clean a new device?
A light wipe is enough. Do not rinse a new device.

## Shop
Browse [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/) and [vape kits](/shop/vape-kits/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## A weekly cleaning routine in ten minutes
Pick one evening a week. Switch the device off and remove the pod or tank. Wipe the outside with a dry cloth. Clean the contacts with a dry cotton bud. Lift lint from the charging port with a wooden toothpick. Rinse the glass and mouthpiece of a tank in warm water, dry them and replace any worn seal. Reassemble when dry, and test. The whole routine is ten minutes, and it keeps the device in good condition. If you cannot manage a weekly routine, do it every two weeks, and wipe the mouthpiece daily.

## Why a clean device is easier to troubleshoot
When a device is clean, problems stand out. A leak is obvious because there is no old liquid to hide it. A bad contact is easy to find because the contacts are bright. A burnt taste points to the coil, not residue in the tank. If you ever need to contact us about a device, a clean one with clear photos makes it easy to help. See [why a vape is not hitting](/blog/why-is-my-vape-not-hitting/) and [what to do when a vape will not charge](/blog/vape-wont-charge-fixes/).

## Cleaning and hygiene
Mouthpieces touch your mouth, so keep them clean, especially if more than one adult uses a household. Do not share devices. Wash your hands before you handle a device, and after you fill or clean it. Nicotine liquid on skin should be washed off with soap and water. Keep cleaning supplies, liquids and devices away from children and pets.

## Cleaning and the environment
Wipe spills with paper towels and dispose of them responsibly, not down the drain. Do not rinse nicotine liquid into the sink. Collect used cotton buds and towels in a bag, and put them in the bin with the lid closed. If you rinse tank parts, use a small amount of warm water, and pour it away with the usual household waste water, after wiping the parts with a paper towel first.

faq.q: How do I clean a vape?
faq.a: Wipe the outside and mouthpiece with a dry cloth, clean contacts with a dry cotton bud and clear lint from the port with a wooden toothpick. Rinse only the tank parts that detach.

faq.q: What must I never get wet?
faq.a: The battery, electronics, charging port and contacts. Never submerge a device or rinse a coil.
Wipe daily, clean contacts weekly, and rinse tanks and check seals monthly or when you change a coil.

faq.q: How do I clean a disposable?
faq.a: Wipe the outside and mouthpiece, and clear lint from the port gently. Do not open or wet it.

faq.q: What do I do about spilled liquid?
faq.a: Wipe it at once with paper towels, wash your hands and the surface and dry the contacts and port before charging.
No. Replace it when flavor fades.
